headline: Integrative omics nominates candidate regulators across cardiac and neural tissues
label: Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis In Disease
summary: Recent studies combine GWAS, eQTL colocalization, single-cell atlases and knockout phenotypes to prioritize disease regulators.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of transcriptomic and multi-omic data as an integrative layer that nominates candidate regulators rather than describing expression alone. Several items pair RNA-seq or single-cell data with external evidence. CHD and ASD GWAS are combined with cardiac and brain cis-eQTLs through colocalization and Mendelian randomization, and CHD7 and MEF2C are then prioritized by machine-learning selection. A logic-based ODE model of cardiomyocyte hypertrophic signaling is linked to IMPC knockout phenotypes, yielding VAV2, RASA1 and LEPR as predicted and validated regulators. Other items apply comparable strategies to cell-state comparisons, including a cross-species, cross-stage conduction system atlas spanning five species, DMD muscle stem cell trajectories, and miRNA-mRNA networks in hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos fibroblasts. What is new is the explicit coupling of cross-species or cross-tissue transcriptomic data to mechanistic or genetic priors, although these studies differ considerably in scope and depth of validation.
